# ARC

1. On a grey autumn morning Emma and Noah stand with Daniel on the misty, wet stones of the quay at the Hafen Enge in Zürich, in the pirate costumes Daniel sewed, pressed in among hundreds of onlookers; Noah says they must reach the front railing before ten, because at ten the bell rings, the lines come in, and the old sailing ship Nebelmöwe sails out for the last time and never again.

2. Emma sees only coats and legs and is impatient, therefore Daniel lifts her onto his shoulders; from up there she sees a woman in a blue coat at the ship's rail who calls down that she has only one deckhand left and needs two more hands at the sail, and Emma says she wants to be one of those hands.

3. The bell rings and the crowd pushes forward, so Emma's tricorn is knocked off her head and disappears under the shoes; Emma is frightened and cross.

4. Emma slides down and crawls between the legs of the grown-ups to look for her hat, but she finds instead a navy-blue captain's cap with a gold anchor, wet from the stones, so she puts it on and is delighted.

5. As she stands up, a boy in a homemade pirate coat is holding her tricorn; he says his name is Kilian, that he pulled the hat out from under the shoes, that he heard the woman call for hands, and that a real captain's cap will prove he belongs on that ship, therefore he demands the trade — but Emma holds the cap with both hands and refuses.

6. At the chestnut stand Hans, who has roasted Marroni beside this quay for years, gives Emma and Noah one hot chestnut each and says that the woman in the blue coat is Kapitänin Sarah, that he saw her lose that cap in the crush, and that she went aboard without knowing where it fell.

7. Emma's hands are full, so she puts her Marroni in her coat pocket and starts to push the cap under her coat, but she stops, because Noah says the owner is standing up there and that whoever carries the cap forward will be seen out of hundreds; Emma is torn, yet she leaves the cap on her head and decides to bring it back.

8. Daniel stays at the stand to pay and forgets to hold on, therefore the next surge shoves him backwards with the dry jackets and the chestnut bag, and he calls that the two should work their way to the rail and wait for him there; Emma is afraid without him.

9. The wall of grown-ups is too thick for Noah, but Emma is small enough to crawl underneath, so Noah tells her to crawl ahead and keep shouting his name; it is dark down there between the legs and Emma is frightened, but she goes.

10. Emma comes out at the front railing as the church clock strikes ten, and Kilian, small enough to use the gap she has opened, squeezes out beside her; Noah forces his way through behind them both.

11. The one deckhand has to haul in the gangway alone, therefore he leaves the last stern line lying loosely looped over the iron bollard and runs forward to the sail, and the Nebelmöwe begins to slide away from the stone edge.

12. Kilian waves the tricorn and shouts, but Kapitänin Sarah is watching the water and not the quay, and the shouting of two children is lost among hundreds of shouting people; Emma is close to tears.

13. Noah seizes the slack line as it slips towards the edge, but one boy alone cannot hold it, and Kilian says he takes orders from nobody's crew and runs to the empty place where the gangway stood; therefore Emma grips the line behind Noah, and together they drag one turn of it around the iron bollard and hold on.

14. The turn holds, so the Nebelmöwe stops a hand's breadth from the stone; Kapitänin Sarah looks over the rail, sees her line stretched down to the bollard and her cap with the gold anchor on the smallest pirate, and has the gangway run out again.

15. Emma climbs up and lays the cap in Sarah's hands herself and says it belongs to her, so Sarah puts it on and takes the two of them aboard as her hands at the sail; Daniel reaches the gangway with the dry jackets, and because Emma will not sail without him, Sarah calls him aboard too.

16. Emma asks for her hat, therefore she throws her hot Marroni down to Kilian, who stands alone beside the empty gangway place and throws the tricorn up to her; Emma wears it at the bow between Noah and Daniel while the black skull sail fills, and she says she is proud, because she gave the cap back with her own hands.

Challenges taken:
1. Reaching the front of a crowd too thick for them.
2. Keeping the found cap or giving it back, with a rival demanding it.
3. Holding the ship at the bollard after it has cast off.
